name: Distributed syscall model for scaling Unix instances

mentions.name: Distributed syscall model for scaling Unix instances
mentions.description: A distributed syscall model that transparently scales Unix instances. Syscalls are translated into batched operations against an underlying non-transactional datastore, and on the service side the database operations are backed by a proxy that serves any desired filesystem or socket interface. Scaling is one motivation; enforcing fine-grained policy on these data operations is another.
mentions.problem: Scaling Unix instances transparently, and enforcing fine-grained policy on data operations
mentions.source_excerpt: I'm finally revisiting a distributed syscall model for transparently scaling unix instances. syscalls get translated into batched operations on an underlying non-transactional datastore. On the service side, database operations get backed by a proxy serving whatever filesystem or socket interface you like. Scaling is one motivation, but the ability to enforce fine-grained policy on these data operations is another big one.
